reason: The text is fundamentally organized around and emphasizes strict hierarchical structures throughout. This includes: (1) genealogical ordering of the tribes with explicit mention of Reuben as 'firstborn of Israel' (בְּכֹר יִשְׂרָאֵל), establishing patrilineal hierarchy; (2) detailed tribal and family hierarchies within the Levites (Gershon, Kohath, Merari as primary divisions with sub-lineages); (3) explicit appointment of Moses and Aaron in hierarchical leadership roles, with Aaron designated as Moses' prophet/spokesman in a subordinate position; (4) clear divine hierarchy with God at the apex issuing commands that flow through Moses and Aaron to the people; (5) patriarchal family structures emphasized through genealogical lineage. The text's very structure and organization demonstrates that hierarchy is not merely present but central to its meaning and purpose.
